facts.text: Wimer was named for a relative of William Wimer, who edited a newspaper in Grants Pass during the late 1880s.
The Wimer Covered Bridge is a historic landmark spanning Evans Creek and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
After the original Wimer Covered Bridge collapsed in 2003, it was rebuilt in 2008 using stronger materials to resemble its predecessor.
Wimer lies along Evans Creek in the southern Oregon foothills, where the fertile bottomlands attracted early European-American settlers.
Improved refrigeration on the Southern Pacific Railroad helped Wimer orchards ship pears and apples to distant markets after 1900.
The Evans Valley Community Center in Wimer hosts local events, exercise classes, and concerts to foster a tight-knit atmosphere.
